title: fabrika config (.fabrika.jsonc)
description: Every key fabrika reads from .fabrika.jsonc. Each is independently optional and falls to its shipped default when absent; this schema documents the shape of a declared value. Generated by `fabrika config schema --write` — edit the key fragments in packages/fabrika-cli/src/config/keys/, never this file.

$schema.description: Path to the JSON Schema for this file — e.g. "./.fabrika.schema.json". Gives an editor autocomplete and validation for the keys below.

boardVocabulary.description: The statuses, types, priorities, audiences and standing lanes this repo's board runs on. Every sub-key is independently optional.

statuses.description: The status role → label map. Every role is optional and falls to its shipped label.

priorities.description: The priority labels triage may keep.

audiences.description: The audience labels triage may keep.

standingLanes.description: The standing-lane labels; an empty list means every issue homes on a milestone.

campaignAuthors.description: Who may declare a campaign or flip its lifecycle state (`fabrika campaign open` / `fabrika campaign state`), narrowing the repository's collaborator ACL — an entry here still needs `write` or above on the repo. Each entry is a GitHub `@user` or `@org/team`, `@`-prefixed. Empty (or absent) means nobody may declare.

capClearAuthors.description: Who may clear one extra repair round on a PR (`fabrika build clear`). Each entry is a GitHub `@user` or `@org/team`, `@`-prefixed. Empty (or absent) means nobody may grant.

ci.description: What fabrika may assume about the repo's continuous-integration producer.

noProducer.description: What a repo with zero Actions workflows gets: `refuse` (a rollup over no producer is vacuous) or `degrade`.

gateWorkflow.description: The CI gate's workflow filename, as `gh api actions/workflows/<file>` names it — a bare filename, not a path.

codeValidators.description: The repo's own commands that compile and lint its code — `build check --surface code` spawns each. Empty (or absent) refuses UNKNOWN rather than guessing a command line.

containmentVocabulary.description: Which child types are asked for a `**Containment:**` marker, and which values satisfy it. An empty half means the marker is never required.

types.description: The `type:` labels a child must carry to be asked for a marker.

values.description: The keywords that satisfy the marker. Never "none", the reserved declination.

cycleDoc.description: The product-development cycle doc a containment class is derived from, repo-relative.

decisionsDir.description: The decision corpus directory, repo-relative. Write null to declare that this repo keeps no decision corpus.

dependencyReconciler.description: The repo's command that installs what its lockfile pins — `lane integrate` runs it in the assembly worktree after a clean child merge, before the code validators. Absent or null runs no install.

docLeakExempt.description: Docs whose subject IS path hygiene — `build check --surface prose` skips its leak scan on them. Repo-relative path suffixes. Empty (or absent) means nothing is exempt.

governedRoots.description: The repo-relative roots a diff derives the governance namespace over. Must cover .fabrika.jsonc itself — a config cannot un-govern itself.

laneConcurrencyCap.description: How many issue lanes may stand open at once — `lane open` and `lane emit` refuse past it, with no override. Write null (or leave it out) for no cap.

portability.description: What `fabrika guard portability-guard check` treats as this repository's own. `repoNames` are the product, org and directory names fabrika's shipped text may not carry; they are matched whole and case-insensitively. Absent or empty means this repo keeps no names of its own out — the guard's four other rules are unaffected.

repoNames.description: Names that resolve only in this repository.

roadmapFile.description: The roadmap file carrying the `## Campaigns` focus table, repo-relative.

surfaceDispositions.description: What this repo does when a surface fabrika reads is missing. Declare only the ids you move; every other falls to its shipped disposition.

triageFacets.description: What each triage facet owns and every label an input can make it keep. A facet declares its ownership as `owns` (a regex) or `ownsLabels` (an explicit set), never both.

values.description: Every label this facet may keep.

owns.description: A regular expression matching the labels this facet has delete authority over.

ownsLabels.description: The explicit set of labels this facet has delete authority over.

uiCapture.description: How a capture of a `uiSurfaces` row is taken: the viewport, where evidence is hosted, and the storage state to browse as.

viewport.description: The capture viewport in CSS px. Defaults to 1280x900.

evidenceStore.description: The evidence store captures are uploaded to. Null (or absent) hosts evidence on GitHub as an attachment.

storageState.description: A repo-relative Playwright storage-state file to browse as. It is a credential — gitignore it, never inline the cookies.

uiSurfaces.description: The runnable apps this repo renders, one row per app. An empty list means no rendered gate: no path raises the ui class and `ui render` refuses.

items.description: One runnable app: where its rendered source lives, how to start it, and what it serves.

name.description: Kebab-case app name, unique across the list.

prefix.description: The repo-relative source root whose changed files raise the ui class, ending in `/`.

mount.description: The prefix of the surface namespace this app owns, unique across the list.

basePath.description: Where this app serves its mounted pages, when that is not the mount itself. Defaults to the mount.

command.description: The shell command that starts the app. Must carry a bare `{{port}}` placeholder; `{{port:<name>}}` allocates further ports.

readyPath.description: The path polled for a 200 before any capture. Defaults to `/`.

unreadableCodeowners.description: What a §CP read does when `.github/CODEOWNERS` itself cannot be read: `ship` treats the boundary as absent, `refuse` raises the caller's UNKNOWN. Nothing reads this key today.

workflowValidators.description: The repo's own commands that machine-read `.github/workflows/**` — `build check --surface workflows` spawns each. Empty (or absent) stands on actionlint alone.

reads.description: The exact workflow files this command opens — what makes a passing run checkable per file.
